rationales: The nucleus does not serve as the main site of cellular respiration.
Mitochondria are the main site of aerobic cellular respiration.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins rather than carry out cellular respiration.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages molecules rather than carry out cellular respiration.
Proteins are primarily synthesized by ribosomes, especially those on rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is primarily involved in lipid synthesis.
Carbohydrates are not the primary product synthesized by smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Nucleic acids are synthesized by enzymes rather than by smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
Ribosomes are made of ribosomal RNA and proteins.
DNA is not a structural component of ribosomes.
Carbohydrates and lipids are not the primary components of ribosomes.
Ribosomes contain RNA, but carbohydrates are not their other main component.
Energy production is primarily associated with mitochondria, not ribosomes.
Ribosomes translate messenger RNA to synthesize proteins.
Lipid synthesis is primarily associated with smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
DNA synthesis is carried out by enzymes, not ribosomes.
The nucleus stores genetic material and does not primarily package and modify proteins.
Mitochondria primarily produce cellular energy rather than package and modify proteins.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins.
The endoplasmic reticulum helps synthesize and transport proteins, but the Golgi apparatus is the primary packaging and modification organelle.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages molecules rather than breaking down cellular waste.
The nucleus contains genetic material and does not primarily break down waste.
Mitochondria produce energy and do not primarily digest waste materials.
Lysosomes contain enzymes that break down waste and cellular materials.
The cytoskeleton helps maintain cell shape and provides structural support.
Centrioles organize microtubules and help with cell division, but are not the primary structures maintaining cell shape.
The nucleus contains genetic material and is not the main structure responsible for cell shape.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials rather than maintain cell shape.
The nucleoplasm is the fluid inside the nucleus, not the main site of ribosome assembly.
The nucleolus is the nuclear region where ribosomal subunits are assembled.
Chromatin is DNA associated with proteins and is not the site of ribosome assembly.
Chromatin is DNA associated with proteins and is not the site of ribosome assembly.
Nuclear pores do not primarily regulate cell division.
Nuclear pores do not control the pH of the cell.
Protein synthesis occurs at ribosomes, not at nuclear pores.
Nuclear pores regulate the movement of molecules between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
The cell membrane surrounds the cell but is not the specialized structure that helps organize cell division.
Centrioles, found in many animal cells, help organize the spindle during cell division.
Plasmodesmata are channels between plant cells, not structures in animal cells.
Vacuoles are storage compartments and are not the animal-cell structure that helps organize division.
The endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes and transports molecules but is not the main site of energy production.
The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages molecules rather than produce most cellular energy.
Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials rather than produce energy.
Xylem primarily transports water and minerals rather than produce glucose.
Phloem primarily transports sugars and other products rather than produce glucose.
Epidermal cells primarily protect the plant and generally are not the main photosynthetic cells.
Mesophyll cells carry out most photosynthesis in leaves, producing glucose.
Ribosomes are assembled from components and do not independently double their number as organelles.
Lysosomes are formed through cellular membrane trafficking and do not independently replicate.
Mitochondria contain their own DNA and can grow and divide to increase their number.
The Golgi apparatus does not independently replicate by dividing.
Ribosomes attached to its surface give rough endoplasmic reticulum its characteristic appearance.
Lysosomes are separate organelles and are not attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum surface.
Mitochondria are separate organelles rather than structures on the rough endoplasmic reticulum surface.
Vacuoles are separate membrane-bound compartments and are not attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum surface.
